title: Grokking
description: Test performance improves long after training performance has saturated.

claims.heading: Algorithmic models can generalize long after memorization, with longer delays on smaller datasets
Gradual circuit formation, then removal of memorizing components, can underlie grokking
Grokking extends beyond algorithmic data, but training controls depend on the setting
Grokking-like delayed generalization occurs during language-model pretraining and fine-tuning
Weight decay favors efficient generalizing circuits over memorization
Networks trained on the same task converge to the same algorithm
Do optimizer and numerical artifacts fully explain the grokking delay?

related_findings.title: Abrupt learning without prior memorization
related_findings.summary: Abrupt capability gains can occur without prior memorization or a gap between training and test performance. Features can develop before these gains, either without visible performance changes or in stages.

examples.headline: Online-trained transformers filling matrix gaps stall at copying, then learn abruptly without a training–test performance gap.

related_findings.title: Algebraic circuits depend on the task
related_findings.summary: Generalizing algorithmic models often learn algebraic representations suited to their tasks. The relevant basis and computation depend on the task and architecture.

examples.headline: Modular-multiplication neurons tune to individual frequencies in multiplicative, rather than additive, Fourier representations.

related_findings.title: Data and capacity separate learning regimes
related_findings.summary: Data coverage and model capacity can separate memorization, delayed generalization and immediate generalization. Such thresholds can arise without explicit weight decay.

examples.headline: Polynomial regression shifts from failed generalization to grokking to simultaneous learning as P increases.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Structure and sampling shape generalization
related_findings.summary: Algebraic structure, input representation and sampling affect whether and when generalization occurs. Training-set size alone does not determine whether held-out examples are recoverable.

examples.headline: Recursive feature machines fail on test points unchanged by reflection; repartitioning training/test data restores high accuracy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Model design controls the delay
related_findings.summary: Architecture, initialization, parameterization and training objectives can shorten, remove or prevent delayed generalization. Learning need not shift from keeping features near their initial values (lazy learning) to changing them substantially (rich learning).

examples.headline: On synthetic KG-QA, shared-access configurations cross the OOD threshold across seeds while Dense never crosses.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Optimization changes speed and reliability
related_findings.summary: Optimizer dynamics and regularization affect grokking timing and reliability. Acceleration methods can interfere with one another or trade speed for stability.

examples.headline: SNR-gated Adam reaches 95% held-out accuracy 4.9× faster than AdamW.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Statistics can reveal progress before accuracy changes
related_findings.summary: Weight, gradient, output and representation statistics can track or precede grokking and distinguish later overfitting. These signals do not by themselves identify a generalizing circuit.

examples.headline: Gradient-cascade dimension separates grokked and ungrokked ModAdd-59 trajectories 100–200 epochs before behavioral grokking.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Representation geometry changes around grokking
related_findings.summary: Representation rank, dimension, clustering and topology can change around grokking. The direction and timing of these changes depend on the task, architecture and measurement.

examples.headline: Last-layer LLID drops with the validation-accuracy jump and reaches lower minima in grokking runs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Total weight norm leaves important differences unresolved
related_findings.summary: Weight norm can affect how long grokking takes, but its trajectory alone is insufficient to explain it. How norm is distributed across layers, activation scale, saturation of pre-softmax outputs (logits) and weight direction also matter.

examples.headline: Redistributing fixed norm between embedding and output layers changes grokking time despite similar pre-softmax output scale.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Regularization can govern the delay before generalization
related_findings.summary: In some regimes, grokking delay follows a clock involving learning rate and decay strength. Excessive regularization and feature learning limit this relationship.

examples.headline: Weight decay applied during only some training steps preserves modular-addition generalization but delays grokking about fivefold.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Different representations can support similar functions
related_findings.summary: Runs can share functions or circuit roles while differing in coordinates, heads or frequencies. Parameter differences alone do not establish different algorithms.

examples.headline: Models with mixed weights behave like whichever source model supplies the retained weight-vector direction.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Early signals need controls
related_findings.summary: A statistic that changes before grokking need not reliably predict it or explain its mechanism. Conclusions depend on null models, the coordinates used for analysis, the measurement window and whether interventions test what they are meant to test.

examples.headline: An eigenvalue-gap detector gives false alarms with short rolling windows in control runs without weight decay.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Internal development continues after accuracy saturates
related_findings.summary: Representations and circuits can keep simplifying, reorganizing or becoming transferable after task accuracy saturates. This later development need not involve delayed behavioral generalization.

examples.headline: T5-Base grammar transfer reaches 90% relative performance 48k steps after in-task performance reaches that level.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Measurement changes how abrupt learning appears
related_findings.summary: Accuracy thresholds, aggregation, plotting axes and evaluation procedures affect the apparent timing and suddenness of grokking. Measurements that vary continuously or separate component contributions can reveal a different trajectory.

examples.headline: POLCA projected-loss clusters better separate carry structure and reveal breakthroughs after the exact-loss plateau.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Complexity measures follow different trajectories
related_findings.summary: Compression, curvature, parameter redundancy (degeneracy) and effective parameter count need not change together. A complexity measure can track training without anticipating generalization.

examples.headline: Reported local learning coefficient, a complexity measure, rises about fourfold before grokking, then plateaus during grokking.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: The transition type remains unresolved
related_findings.summary: Statistical-physics accounts describe grokking through non-equilibrium dynamics, barrier crossing and finite-size transitions. The evidence does not establish a universal transition order or escape mechanism.

examples.headline: Extrapolated transition-type estimates vary across sampling grids, remaining inconclusive despite single-peaked distributions across seeds.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Gradient allocation shapes generalization
related_findings.summary: Gradient direction, competition that prevents some features from learning, and interactions between modules affect grokking. The evidence does not support a universal shift from MLPs memorizing to attention generalizing.

examples.headline: Boosting non-commutativity accelerates Dyck grokking, while a kick prevents SCAN grokking.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generalization can appear, disappear and return
related_findings.summary: Rules and transferable solutions can appear before memorization and later be displaced by memorization or competing priors. Capability changes can reverse during training.

examples.headline: OLMo3-32B Successive Answer answer+1 accuracy falls from 81% to zero before recovering to 81.7%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Task structure and supervision can shorten delays
related_findings.summary: Task-compatible representations, symmetries and intermediate supervision can shorten or remove grokking. Incompatible structural constraints can prevent it.

examples.headline: For COMPARISON, k=3 Max, ϕ=3.6, CoT supervision advances OOD take-off from 120K to 16K steps.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generalization can deteriorate after grokking
related_findings.summary: Generalization can relapse or collapse during continued training. Stability depends on optimizer updates, regularization, numerical effects and subsequent data.

examples.headline: Modular-addition test accuracy declines after grokking while training accuracy remains perfect.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Capabilities and steering develop on different schedules
related_findings.summary: Language-model capabilities, transferable representations and steering efficacy can develop at different times. Abrupt late changes alone do not establish a memorization-to-generalization gap.

examples.headline: Dialogue-tuned CrystalCoder checkpoints respond sharply more to steering toward anger after about 68% of pretraining steps.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Learned components can accelerate new tasks
related_findings.summary: Learned algorithmic components can transfer or compose to accelerate generalization. Transfer depends on the operation, representation and component position.

examples.headline: Transferring trained decoders accelerates multiplication; transferring embeddings lets three-operand addition reach the required test accuracy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Information and uncertainty follow distinct schedules
related_findings.summary: Information, entropy and uncertainty measures can show peaks, reversals and compression phases around grokking. Their timing depends on the metric.

examples.headline: Under Gaussian VI, Bayesian linear regression shows growing accuracy and uncertainty-peak delays as λ approaches 1.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Loss spikes do not uniquely explain generalization
related_findings.summary: Slingshot loss spikes and optimizer oscillations can accompany changes in learned representations and improved generalization. Spikes alone neither predict grokking nor establish a unique beneficial mechanism.

examples.headline: On sparse parity, slingshots and matched random perturbations produce loss improvements with no statistically significant difference.

related_findings.title: Label noise changes the path to generalization
related_findings.summary: Label noise can delay or block grokking and change the order of fitting clean and corrupted labels. Recovery depends on corruption structure, optimization history and which labels are corrected.

examples.headline: Uniform training-label noise delays grokking, with measurable effects even at 0.5% noise.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Initialization helps determine which features survive
related_findings.summary: Initialization and the frequency content of input encodings partly determine which generalizing features survive training. They also influence the order in which Fourier components are learned.

examples.headline: Fourier-circle survival correlates with initial signal, and perturbing that signal changes survival.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Flatness alone does not ensure generalization
related_findings.summary: Flatness can correlate with or modify grokking, but it is insufficient on its own. Flatness measures that change when the same model is expressed with different parameters need not determine when grokking starts.

examples.headline: Runs using only sharpness-aware minimization fail to generalize despite the lowest curvature by maximum Hessian eigenvalue.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Success on one split can hide extrapolation failures
related_findings.summary: A learned algorithmic solution can succeed within its evaluation split yet fail on longer sequences, new formats or deeper compositions. Broader extrapolation depends on architecture and invariance training.

examples.headline: Text-rendered modular addition reaches 96.8% disjoint-pair accuracy but fails under position shifts and new templates.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Delayed generalization extends beyond standard neural settings
related_findings.summary: Delayed generalization also occurs in linear, kernel and matrix-completion settings. Neural feature learning, adaptive optimizers, softmax and explicit weight decay are not universal requirements.

examples.headline: Multiplication-table matrix completion minimizes training loss long before its sharp test-loss transition.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generalizing structure can coexist with memorization
related_findings.summary: Subnetworks, masks or frequency filtering can recover generalizing structure from models that also memorize. Sparsity alone does not explain this recovery.

examples.headline: Filtering frequency components post-training recovers near-perfect test accuracy under 80% label noise, without establishing delayed generalization.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Accurate solutions can differ in robustness
related_findings.summary: Robustness can develop after clean generalization and differ between equally accurate solutions. Behavioral grokking alone does not establish resistance to perturbations or forgetting.

examples.headline: After noise memorization, WLMD-equilibrium models retain higher original-task accuracy than AdamW-goldilocks at equal weight norm.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fewer updates need not mean greater efficiency
related_findings.summary: Acceleration measured in updates need not improve sample or compute efficiency. Dataset-size effects depend on whether updates, epochs, examples or FLOPs are held fixed.

examples.headline: Batch size 512 reaches the threshold within the step budget, not the example budget.

related_findings.title: Numerical choices can change individual outcomes
related_findings.summary: Finite-precision choices can cause loss spikes or change individual grokking outcomes. Aggregate grokking rates can remain unchanged despite these differences.

examples.headline: Reordering how CPUs combine results or switching CPU/GPU flips individual grokking outcomes without detectable overall-rate shifts.

reading_list.why: Establishes the original behavioral baseline: prolonged generalization delay after memorization on small algorithmic datasets.
Connects modular-addition grokking to Fourier computation, measurable progress before the test transition, and later sparsification.
Tests identifiable computation through causal abstraction beyond modular addition and challenges uniformly gradual circuit formation.

known_gaps.summary: Open questions concern measuring the delay between memorization and generalization directly, reproducing results under matched conditions at scale, numerical effects, checking figures, study independence, and what norm and representation evidence reveals about mechanisms.
items: It remains unresolved whether shrinking the training set lengthens the gap after training accuracy saturates under fixed task and optimizer conditions. Time to a validation threshold does not establish that relationship.

Large-language-model studies use different definitions and protocols, leaving replication under matched conditions unresolved. Pretraining evidence relies on pairings chosen after the fact and evaluation after instruction tuning, while fine-tuning that injects facts includes failures to generalize.

It remains unclear how much numerical effects contribute to slingshots, the repeated sudden loss spikes late in training. Higher precision can remove spikes, and changing the order of floating-point sums can change whether individual runs grok.

Some conclusions about loss of generalization after reducing training data, algorithm differences across runs and the causes of loss spikes rest on training curves that could not be fully checked. The supporting figures were only partly accessible.

Some supporting studies share authors, may duplicate the same work, or measure an original study’s saved model again, so their independence remains unresolved. Several proposed generalizations still need confirmation from independent studies.

Disagreements about controlling weight magnitude remain hard to interpret because studies differ in when they project weights back to a chosen norm and in other experimental conditions. These comparisons do not yet isolate when controlling weight magnitude governs grokking.

The geometry of learned representations, embedding spectra (how variation is distributed across directions), and concentration at particular Fourier frequencies in the final model do not establish when a generalizing computation forms or whether runs learn different algorithms.
